title: 8 Perfect Sci-Fi TV Shows Set in Space: Farscape, The Expanse, and More
text:
From Farscape to The Expanse, discover eight sci-fi TV shows set in space that are considered perfect, featuring groundbreaking storytelling and world-building.
Science fiction television has produced many exceptional shows, but several of the greatest of all time are set in outer space. The cosmos has long been a fascinating setting for sci-fi stories, which explains why series like The Expanse and Battlestar Galactica have found such success telling stories among the stars. Over the years, eight particular series have proven that a sci-fi show set in space can be genuinely perfect, earning a 10/10 rating and standing the test of time.
Farscape: A Cult Classic Space Opera
Created by Rockne S. O'Bannon and co-produced by Hallmark and The Jim Henson Company, the Australian space sci-fi show Farscape is among the biggest cult classics that sci-fi television has ever produced. It tells the story of John Crichton (Ben Browder), a modern-day American astronaut who accidentally gets sucked through a wormhole into a distant part of the universe, where he joins a starship's crew while running from a ruthless military empire.
Farscape is frequently hailed as one of the most perfect space opera masterpieces that the small screen has ever seen. Delectably weird and chaotic in all the right ways, it features exquisite and downright groundbreaking practical special effects, world-building of the utmost narrative depth, and character dynamics that allow the show to convey an awful ton of heart. It has the perfect blend between absurdist camp and genuinely dramatic storytelling.
The show ran from 1999 to 2003 and remains one of those classic sci-fi shows that are still worth binge-watching today. Its unique blend of humor, drama, and innovative puppetry has made it a beloved entry in the genre.
The Expanse: Masterful Scientific Realism
Based on the series of novels of the same name by James S. A. Corey (the pen name of Daniel Abraham and Ty Franck), The Expanse is one of the most perfect sci-fi shows worth watching over and over again. It takes place in a colonized solar system on the brink of war between Earth, Mars, and the asteroid belt, following a rogue ship crew and a hardened detective who stumble upon a dangerous alien conspiracy.
Widely praised as one of the modern hard sci-fi shows with the most masterful scientific realism, The Expanse is a neo-noir space opera that feels unlike anything else the genre has produced in years. Without having produced a single bad episode over the course of six exceptional seasons, it spent that time building deeply human character arcs and a plot infused with sweeping political complexity, stunning world-building, and grounded themes.
The series aired from 2015 to 2022 and has become a benchmark for contemporary science fiction television.
Babylon 5: A Novel for Television
In the history of not only science fiction television, but American broadcast television as a whole, there's a before Babylon 5 and an after Babylon 5. In a twist that was quite unusual at the time, this space opera was devised as an almost entirely serialized novel for television, where each season would serve as a chapter in that novel. The story follows a space station in the mid-23rd century, which becomes a diplomatic hub for a massive galactic war and a struggle against human totalitarianism.
Though such an intense level of serialization was almost unprecedented for American cable television at the time, Babylon 5 has nevertheless aged beautifully, and is still one of those classic sci-fi shows better than most new series. On top of being highly influential, its quasi-Shakespearean, mature political realism, timeless themes, and brilliantly constructed character arcs make it irresistibly entertaining from beginning to end.
The show originally aired from 1994 to 1998 and remains a landmark achievement in serialized storytelling.
Andor: A Gripping Space Thriller
Going into 2022, people were, at best, skeptical about Andor. After all, how good could a spin-off prequel show to a spin-off prequel movie really be? In the end, it turned out that the answer was really damn good. There are those, in fact, who would confidently say that this gripping space thriller about the eponymous thief (Diego Luna) turning into a dedicated revolutionary is the best that the Star Wars franchise has been since Disney's acquisition of Lucasfilm.
One of those sci-fi shows that are perfect for a weekend binge, Andor may only be 24 episodes long, but it's such a sprawling and ambitious critique of fascist violence and authoritarian oppression that its effects last a lifetime. It's both perfectly written and technically perfect, a combination that the franchise as a whole has remarkably rarely seen to this admirable a degree.
The series aired from 2022 to 2025 and has been praised for its mature tone and complex characters.
